newsitem.title: USA: Microbrewers fizzle after Boston Beer profits fall.
newsitem.headline: Microbrewers fizzle after Boston Beer profits fall.

text.p: Microbrewery stocks took a nosedive on Wednesday after industry leader Boston Beer Co. Inc., maker of Samuel Adams beers, said its orders were lower than expected.
A selling wave sheared 20 percent off Boston Beer after the company said October/November 1996 orders grew only 5.5 percent over shipments for the same period last year.

The stock lost $3.50 to $12.50, an all-time low, on the New York Stock Exchange. Boston Beer made the forecast in its third quarter earnings announcement on Tuesday. It posted earnings of $2.3 million, or 11 cents a share vs. $1.8 million, or 10 cents a share, a year earlier.
"The (third-quarter) earnings were in line ... but they're not looking good for the fourth quarter. The whole area is slowing down," said Wheat First Butcher Singer Inc. analyst John Maxwell.
Wall Street's pessimism was likely to continue for the next year or so on increased industry competition and the growth slowdown, he said.
Three brokerage firms promptly downgraded the stock, with Dean Witter cropping earnings estimates as prospects for future growth dimmed.

Industry rivals also tumbled. Redhook Ale Brewery Inc. fell $1.31, or 8 percent, to $14.69, and Pete's Brewing Co. lost 37.5 cents, or 5 percent, to $7.375. Pyramid Breweries Inc. and Nor'Wester Brewing Co. also fell.

The blow came as a sharp contrast to last year, when Boston Beer was the toast of the market, surging more than 50 percent on its first day of trading to $30.375 after its initial public offering and later hitting a high of $33.

"With the Northeast, Washington and Oregon with a 10 percent share and the rest of the country at about 2 percent, some felt there was a possibility the rest of the country could move up to 10," Maxwell said. "But now they're thinking maybe that won't be the share these companies take over time."
The industry has made some disappointing announcements since last year, when most of the major players appeared on the market amidst high fanfare.
Redhook, Pete's Brewing and Pyramid Breweries all said earlier this fall they expected disappointing third-quarter results.
